title: Revenue Recognition Overview
description: Understand the core principle and five-step revenue recognition model.
html:
The core principle

Revenue recognition is based on the transfer of promised goods or services to customers.

Revenue should reflect the amount of consideration the company expects to receive in exchange for those goods or services.

The five-step model

  1. Identify the contract with a customer.
  2. Identify the performance obligations.
  3. Determine the transaction price.
  4. Allocate the transaction price.
  5. Recognize revenue when or as each performance obligation is satisfied.

Simple example

A company agrees to sell a customer a laptop for $1,500.

The laptop is transferred to the customer, and the customer obtains control of it.

Revenue Recognized = $1,500

Why cash timing is not enough

Receiving cash does not automatically mean revenue should be recognized immediately.

Advance payment

A customer pays $12,000 today for services that will be provided over the next 12 months.

The company has received cash, but it has not yet provided all of the promised services.

Revenue recognition depends on satisfying the performance obligation, not merely receiving cash.

Important

Revenue recognition focuses on the transfer of promised goods or services and customer control.

quiz.prompt: Under the revenue recognition model, revenue is recognized primarily when:

choices.text: A performance obligation is satisfied by transferring a promised good or service
Management decides it wants to report revenue

quiz.explanation: Revenue is recognized when or as a performance obligation is satisfied through transfer of the promised good or service to the customer.
